question.text: Milestone Valuation in a Cat I/II AIF term sheet is used primarily because:

answer.text: VC investors want to reward founders for exceeding forecast
SEBI mandates milestone valuation for all Cat I AIF investments
Investors are uncertain about forecast-based valuation and prefer to peg valuation to technical/commercial targets; missing milestones can trigger a valuation downward revision or downround
Tax authorities require milestone valuation under Section 56(2)(viib)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 11.6.1 (Milestone Valuation), VC investors often won't agree to forecast-based valuation at investment time because they don't know when the company will reach profitability. Milestones peg valuation to technical/commercial targets. Missing a milestone doesn't auto-trigger non-funding but can cause downward revision, downround, or delay. The Trap: Option A inverts the logic. Option C is false (SEBI doesn't mandate). Option D misreads tax law. Cross-Exam Context: Milestone valuation crosses XIX-A (product) and tax-oriented questions in Section 56(2)(viib) Angel Tax territory. Manager's Pro-Tip: Milestones must be objective and observable (e.g., 'ARR of INR 50 cr validated by Big-4 auditor'). Subjective milestones ('customer satisfaction improvement') are unenforceable and just create post-hoc disputes.
